method: Seed the same 128 independent keys into hash-bucket Durable Objects at partition counts 1/2/4/8/16/32/64/128. After disposing and reopening the Miniflare runtime with the same SQLite persistence, issue 128 unique cold pointed reads in a single concurrent wave for each layout. Buckets reconstruct a bounded latest-value Map from append-only facts. No retries.
interpretation: At 128 independent cold reads, fewer key buckets improved local p99 in this workload, likely by avoiding a cold-start storm across 128 simultaneously activated DOs. Bucket counts 1 through 64 stayed below 100 ms p99 in all three trials. One of three 128-bucket trials landed at 100 ms (max 101 ms), so the strict target was not reliable at one actor per key. This is not a hosted capacity result; the single-bucket case is a throughput bottleneck risk under sustained/hot traffic.
limitations: Local Miniflare/SQLite, three closed-loop single-wave trials on one machine.
No open-loop/sustained workload, failure injection, tenant churn or hosted placement.
Keys in distinct buckets have independent histories; cross-bucket transactions, joins and snapshots are not provided.
Write p99 increases with bucket count due many cold actors; this summary focuses on read latency.
